records.c: Relocates the picture unpacker to the stack page and low RAM, changes the CPU port and jumps to the unpacker at $0100. The picture paths enter it at $0813.
Banks out I/O and ROMs. Relocates two 166-byte source windows into low memory, then jumps to the unpacker at $0100.
The first copy reads $082A plus Y. The loop stops before Y equals zero, so its first actual source byte is $082B.
Garage briefing package offsets $0019–$0418. This span starts with bytes relocated into low RAM by the bootstrap and continues into the packed picture stream.

The bootstrap at $081F copies $08D1–$0976 to $0334–$03D9 for the unpacker. These bytes are in the packed garage briefing package. The rest of this span supplies the picture decoder until the next boundary at $0C00.
On entry this holds the packed first picture. After the depacker runs, $0C00 is the expanded VIC screen-attribute source.
Packed garage briefing data at package offsets $0419–$0818. The picture unpacker reads these bytes while populating the colour, screen-attribute and bitmap planes.
On entry these bytes still belong to the packed first picture. Expanded bitmap output occupies $1000 after the depacker runs.

The last 192 bytes in the page-aligned bitmap staging region. The 8,000-byte rendered plane ends at $2F3F. The full-page display copies may transfer part of this zero tail beyond the visible cells.
Sets up the display and music, resets SP and makes its first bitmap display call.
Pushes $68FF as the loader return address, selects two blocks of driving file one and jumps to $0433.
Eight zero-filled bytes after the first-stage loader jump and before the low-bank picture-copy helper.
Copies packed data to $0812, depacks it and selects the low VIC bank after transferring the attributes, bitmap and colour RAM planes.
Sets the source and destination operands to copy four pages of colour values to $D800 before selecting the display bank.
Stages and decompresses a picture, then builds a multicolour bitmap using screen RAM under $DC00 and bitmap RAM at $E000.
Increments the VIC border colour and jumps to its own entry, forming a visible diagnostic loop.
Selects the two-byte address from the scene table. The next-picture path increments the index.
Little-endian source addresses for the 4 packed picture programs. The selector indexes with twice the scene number and copies the selected source beginning at $0812.
This base reads the high byte of the picture address at twice the selected scene index. The corresponding low byte is read one address earlier.
Stored $FFFF immediately after the 4 valid picture addresses.
Uses the scene number to select a two-byte source pointer and copies 23 pages into the staging area beginning at $0812.
Low byte of the packed-picture copy’s source operand, set from the selected scene pointer.
High byte of the packed-picture source. The copy increments this after each 256-byte page.
Page byte of the destination operand. Resets to $08 for each picture and advances after each copied page.
Calls the picture depacker at $0813 and restores $35 in the CPU port so the display routines can access I/O.
Copies X plus one full pages to the selected display plane. Increments the source and destination pages as each page completes.
High source operand for the display copy. The caller selects $08, $0C or $10 according to the plane.
High destination operand for the page copier, selected by expected display plane and VIC bank.
Advances through a raster wait loop. Checks the joystick fire line and uses $31B1 to skip only on a fresh press.
Lets a new fire press skip the active delay once. The wait routine clears the latch after release.
Waits for raster low byte zero and then for it to become nonzero.
Clears the I/O address range $D400–$D7FF, then zeros $02–$FF. Preserves the processor port bytes $00 and $01.
High-byte operand that the I/O clear loop increments up to $D8.
Loads the bank, sprite pointer bias, multicolour palette and frame limit and displays the records in order, with a delay before advances.
Copies the frame delay into $0E and counts transitions out of raster line low byte $F1 until the delay expires.
Computes 24 times the 16-bit frame index as eight times plus sixteen times, then adds the sequence table address.
Immediate operand holding the incoming X during frame-record address calculation.
Programs each of eight sprite slots from its three parallel arrays for the selected frame. Tests Y=$FF to leave a slot disabled and reads the shape flags after 63 bytes of pixels.
Operand of the addition that translates the per-slot shape index into a VIC pointer, patched for the sequence.
High byte of the indexed sprite-pointer store. The sequence chooses the low or high VIC bank’s screen pointer page.
Converts the 8-bit VIC sprite pointer in A into a 16-bit byte offset in $0B/$0C using two right shifts and rotations.
High operand patched for reading a sprite shape’s expansion and palette flags in the selected VIC bank.
Eight powers of two used to update the VIC enable, expansion and multicolour flags for each sprite slot.
Low byte of the sprite frame-table address. Stored sequence values are $4E.
High byte of the sprite frame-table address. Stored sequence values are $97.
Number of raster waits per animation step, copied to $0D. Stored sequence values are $04.
Highest frame index the playback loop selects. Stored sequence values are $08.
Patched high byte of the VIC screen’s sprite-pointer store. Stored sequence values are $DF.
Value added to each raw shape index before programming the display pointer. Stored sequence values are $50.
Number of frame delays used to hold the first frame before advancing. Stored sequence values are $14.
Number of frame delays used to hold the final frame before returning. Stored sequence values are $00.
Page bias for reading a sprite’s flag byte from the selected VIC bank. Stored sequence values are $C0.
Value programmed into $D025 when this sequence begins. Stored sequence values are $02.
Value programmed into $D026 when this sequence begins. Stored sequence values are $0F.
Configures the CPU port, masks both CIAs, disables VIC IRQs and silences SID master volume while changing the image.
Points the IRQ at $BE59 and the NMI at $BE91. Acknowledges VIC raster status and enables the IRQ at line 200.
Loader-written zero bytes between the IRQ setup routine and the video-rate wrapper at $3400.
Tests $02A6 and can redirect the raster’s music call to the scene divider. Then quiets the machine for the scene.
The wrapper at $3400 installs this target when $02A6 is zero. Decrements the countdown operand at $3414 and calls $B003. When it expires, reloads six and returns.
Immediate byte used as the divider countdown. It is decremented until the update is skipped and the counter is reloaded.
